title: Virtual Convergence Industry Promotion Act
full_text:
Virtual Convergence Industry Promotion Act

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the development of the national economy and the improvement of the quality of life of the people by prescribing matters necessary for the promotion and support of the virtual convergence industry and the improvement of regulations.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. The term "virtual convergence world (metaverse)" means a virtual space or a space combining the virtual and the real that is structured to enable various social, economic, and cultural activities based on technology that enables interaction between humans and digital information by extending users' five senses into virtual space or blending them with real space (hereinafter referred to as "virtual convergence technology") (hereinafter referred to as a "virtual convergence world").
2. The term "virtual convergence industry" means an industry related to the development, production, release, sale, provision, leasing, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "development, etc.") of services, devices, products, etc. related to virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence worlds (hereinafter referred to as "virtual convergence services, etc.").
3. The term "virtual convergence business entity" means a person engaging in business related to the virtual convergence industry.
4. The term "user" means a person who uses virtual convergence services, etc. provided by a virtual convergence business entity.
5. The term "interim standards" means standards established temporarily to ensure consistent enforcement of statutes and regulations where the applicability or scope of application of statutes and regulations is unclear because their provisions concerning the release, sale, or use of virtual convergence services, etc. are unclear.

Article 3 (Duties of the State)
(1) The State shall formulate and implement policies for the sound and sustainable development of the virtual convergence industry and the creation of an environment for the safe use of virtual convergence services, etc.
(2) The State shall endeavor to promote mutually beneficial cooperation and harmonious development among large enterprises, small and medium enterprises, and venture businesses related to the virtual convergence industry.
(3) The State shall endeavor to enable the people to freely use virtual convergence services, etc. despite physical, economic, social, or other constraints.
(4) Where the State intends to enter into a procurement contract concerning the development, etc. of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc. to promote the virtual convergence industry, it shall endeavor to increase opportunities for small and medium enterprises under Article 2 (1) of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises to receive contracts.
(5) The State shall formulate and implement policies to promote the use of public data under the Act on Promotion of the Provision and Use of Public Data in order to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(6) The State shall formulate and implement policies necessary to promote the virtual convergence industry through convergence between that industry and other industries.

Article 4 (Principle of Permission First and Ex Post Regulation)
(1) Any person may engage in activities related to the development, etc. of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc.: Provided, That the State and local governments may restrict such activities where the use of virtual convergence worlds is likely to significantly undermine public safety and order.
(2) The State and local governments shall endeavor to ensure that statutes, regulations, and systems related to the virtual convergence industry are brought into conformity with the principle under paragraph (1).

Article 5 (Relationship with Other Acts)
Except as otherwise specifically provided in other Acts concerning the promotion of the virtual convergence industry, this Act shall apply.

CHAPTER II SYSTEM FOR PROMOTING THE VIRTUAL CONVERGENCE INDUSTRY

Article 6 (Formulation of Master Plans, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT may formulate and implement a master plan for the virtual convergence industry (hereinafter referred to as "master plan") every three years to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(2) The Minister of Science and ICT shall formulate a master plan by soliciting opinions from the heads of relevant central administrative agencies (including agencies under the President and agencies under the Prime Minister; hereinafter the same shall apply) and the heads of local governments, and shall finalize the plan following deliberation by the Information and Communications Strategy Committee under Article 7 of the Special Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Technology, Vitalization of Convergence Thereof, Etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "Strategy Committee"): Provided, That this shall not apply to changes to minor matters in a master plan prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) A master plan shall include the following matters:
1. The direction and objectives of policies for promoting the virtual convergence industry;
2. The establishment of human and physical infrastructure for promoting the virtual convergence industry, including the fostering of professional personnel and investment in facilities;
3. Support for research and development, dissemination of research outcomes, and promotion of commercialization to advance the virtual convergence industry;
4. Improvement of regulations, laws, and systems for promoting the virtual convergence industry;
5. Cooperation in policies and affairs among relevant central administrative agencies or between relevant central administrative agencies and local governments;
6. Securing and allocating financial resources for promoting the virtual convergence industry;
7. Other matters necessary for promoting the virtual convergence industry.
(4) The Minister of Science and ICT may formulate and implement annual implementation plans under a master plan (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plans").
(5) Where necessary to formulate master plans and implementation plans, the Minister of Science and ICT may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and the heads of relevant organizations and institutions to submit materials. In such cases, the head of a relevant central administrative agency, the head of a local government, or the head of a relevant organization or institution requested to submit materials shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(6) Matters necessary for the formulation and implementation of master plans and implementation plans, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Securing Financial Resources)
The Minister of Science and ICT may support relevant projects from the budget, the Broadcasting Communications Development Fund under Article 24 of the Framework Act on Broadcasting Communications Development, and the Information and Communications Promotion Fund under Article 41 of the Information and Communications Industry Promotion Act to promote the virtual convergence industry.

Article 8 (Fact-Finding Surveys, etc.)
(1) The Government may conduct fact-finding surveys concerning the formulation and implementation of master plans and implementation plans, the current status of related industries for promoting the virtual convergence industry, the identification of tasks for regulatory improvement, etc., and may publish the results.
(2) The head of a central administrative agency may request the heads of other central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as "public institutions"), business entities, enterprises, associations, research institutions, etc. to submit necessary materials or provide support for fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1).
(3) The heads of central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and the heads of public institutions who receive a request under paragraph (2) shall comply unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so.
(4) Matters necessary for fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1) and for the submission of materials and provision of support under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER III ESTABLISHMENT OF INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE VIRTUAL CONVERGENCE INDUSTRY

Article 9 (Reporting of Virtual Convergence Platform Business)
(1) A person operating a virtual convergence platform (hereinafter referred to as a "virtual convergence platform operator") whose sales, etc. meet the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree shall file a report with the Minister of Science and ICT. The same shall apply where such person intends to change an important matter prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT among the matters reported.
(2) The Minister of Science and ICT shall issue a certificate of receipt of a report no later than the day following the date of receipt of a report or a report of changes under paragraph (1): Provided, That where supplementation has been requested under Article 40 (3) of the Administrative Procedures Act, the certificate of receipt shall be issued no later than the day following the date on which supplementation is completed.
(3) Matters necessary concerning the contents, methods, procedures, etc. of reporting under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT.

Article 10 (Fostering of Professional Personnel, etc.)
(1) The Government may formulate and implement the following policies to foster professional personnel required for the virtual convergence industry:
1. Establishment of a system for fostering professional personnel for the virtual convergence industry;
2. Fostering of outstanding professional personnel through industry-academia cooperation and specialized educational institutions;
3. Designation and operation of universities, graduate schools, and university-affiliated research institutes specializing in the virtual convergence industry;
4. Retraining of technical personnel;
5. Other matters necessary for fostering professional personnel.
(2) The Government may provide persons carrying out projects under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) with support for all or part of the costs necessary to carry out the relevant projects, within budgetary limits.
(3) Matters necessary for the formulation and implementation of policies under paragraph (1) and for support under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Promotion of Technology Development)
(1) The Government may implement the following projects to promote the development and advancement of virtual convergence technology:
1. Surveys of trends and levels of virtual convergence technology in Korea and abroad and of related systems;
2. Research, development, testing, and evaluation of virtual convergence technology;
3. Practical application of technology, including cooperation in and transfer of virtual convergence technology;
4. Facilitation of the distribution of information on virtual convergence technology;
5. Other projects necessary for the development of virtual convergence technology.
(2) Where necessary to efficiently implement projects under paragraph (1), the Government may entrust the projects under the subparagraphs of that paragraph to a dedicated agency under Article 17 or a relevant institution or organization.
(3) The Government and local governments may provide persons entrusted with projects under paragraph (2) with support for all or part of the costs necessary to carry out the relevant projects, within budgetary limits.
(4) Matters necessary concerning the scope of affairs entrusted under paragraph (2), the methods and procedures for selecting entrusted institutions, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Establishment of Research and Development Infrastructure)
(1) The Government shall endeavor to establish an institutional foundation for the use of personnel, facilities, equipment, funds, information, etc. to promote research and development related to the virtual convergence industry.
(2) The Government may provide persons conducting research and development related to the virtual convergence industry with support for all or part of the costs of such research and development.

Article 13 (Standardization)
(1) The Government may implement the following projects for standardization related to technology, communications, security, compatibility, interoperability, etc. concerning virtual convergence services, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "standardization"): Provided, That where Korean Industrial Standards under the Industrial Standardization Act have been established, those standards shall be followed.
1. Establishment, revision, abolition, and dissemination of standards;
2. Survey, research, and development of domestic and foreign standards;
3. Other projects necessary for standardization.
(2) The Government may publicly notify standards established under paragraph (1) 1 and recommend them to relevant business entities.
(3) The Government may entrust affairs concerning standardization to a dedicated agency under Article 17 or a relevant institution or organization. In such cases, the Government may provide support necessary for the entrusted institution or organization to perform standardization affairs.
(4) Other matters necessary for standardization shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Upgrading Wired and Wireless Networks)
The Minister of Science and ICT shall endeavor to upgrade wired and wireless networks so that various virtual convergence technologies or virtual convergence services, etc. can be provided reliably.

Article 15 (Financial Support)
The State and local governments may provide loans or investments of necessary funds to virtual convergence business entities or provide other necessary support.

Article 16 (Support for Startups and Private Investment)
The Government may provide necessary support, including assistance with expenses and funding, for startup activities utilizing virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc., and for private investment in such activities.

Article 17 (Designation and Operation of Dedicated Agencies)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT may designate a dedicated agency (hereinafter referred to as a "dedicated agency") to efficiently implement policies for the promotion of the virtual convergence industry.
(2) A dedicated agency shall carry out the following projects:
1. Analysis, provision, and sharing of statistics and information related to the virtual convergence industry;
2. Identification, planning, and support in relation to the virtual convergence industry;
3. Support for pilot projects, demonstration projects, and improvements to laws and systems related to the virtual convergence industry;
4. Support for overseas expansion and international cooperation related to the virtual convergence industry;
5. Management and supervision of virtual convergence industry support centers under Article 19;
6. Other projects prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) The Minister of Science and ICT may make contributions or provide subsidies from the budget, the Broadcasting Communications Development Fund under Article 24 of the Framework Act on Broadcasting Communications Development, and the Information and Communications Promotion Fund under Article 41 of the Information and Communications Industry Promotion Act to cover expenses necessary for the operation of a dedicated agency and the performance of the projects specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (2).
(4) The Minister of Science and ICT may revoke the designation of a dedicated agency if it falls under any of the following subparagraphs; provided that the Minister shall revoke its designation if it falls under subparagraph 1:
1. Where it has obtained designation by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where it has become unable to meet the requirements for designation under paragraph (5);
3. Where it has otherwise become manifestly inappropriate for it to perform its duties as a dedicated agency.
(5) Other matters necessary for the requirements for designation of dedicated agencies and their designation, revocation of designation, support, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Associations)
(1) Virtual convergence business entities may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, establish an association related to the virtual convergence industry (hereinafter referred to as an "association") with authorization from the Minister of Science and ICT, for the sustainable development of the virtual convergence industry through the promotion and expansion of the use of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc., self-regulation, user protection, and other means.
(2) An association shall be a corporation.
(3) An association may perform the following duties:
1. Promoting and expanding the use of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc.;
2. Self-regulation under Article 27;
3. Proposing improvements to systems related to the virtual convergence industry;
4. Training specialized personnel;
5. Protecting users and intellectual property rights;
6. Operating a single point of contact for comprehensive support for regulatory improvements;
7. Other projects necessary to achieve the purposes for which the association was established.
(4) The Minister of Science and ICT may support the performance of the duties under paragraph (3) to promote the virtual convergence industry and for related purposes.

Article 19 (Regional Virtual Convergence Industry Support Centers)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT may designate an institution, organization, or corporation that meets requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree, including specialized personnel and facilities, as a virtual convergence industry support center (hereinafter referred to as a "support center") to efficiently support the promotion of the virtual convergence industry in each region.
(2) A support center shall carry out projects entrusted by the Minister of Science and ICT that are necessary to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(3) The Minister of Science and ICT may, within budgetary limits, provide support for all or part of the expenses necessary for a support center to carry out the projects under paragraph (2).
(4) Where a person designated as a support center falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister of Science and ICT may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, revoke the designation or order the suspension of its duties for a specified period not exceeding six months; provided that the Minister shall revoke the designation where the person falls under subparagraph 1:
1. Where it has obtained designation by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where it has continuously failed to perform its duties for at least six months without good cause;
3. Where it no longer meets the requirements for designation under paragraph (1);
4. Where the support center has used funds provided under paragraph (3) for purposes other than those for which the support was provided.
(5) Other matters necessary for the designation and operation of support centers, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER IV PROMOTION OF THE VIRTUAL CONVERGENCE INDUSTRY

Article 20 (Support for Virtual Convergence Business Entities)
(1) The Government and local governments may provide the following administrative and financial support to virtual convergence business entities to promote the virtual convergence industry:
1. Support for the development of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc., and dissemination of research and development results;
2. Joint use of equipment, facilities, etc.;
3. Support for the commercialization of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc.;
4. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(2) Matters necessary for the support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 21 (Support Projects for the Virtual Convergence Industry)
The heads of central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments may carry out the following projects to promote the virtual convergence industry:
1. Research projects;
2. Projects to establish a foundation for stimulating the industry and to improve systems;
3. Projects to ensure compatibility and interoperability and establish linkages;
4. Projects to support the conversion of existing services, etc. into virtual convergence services, etc.;
5. Other projects necessary to promote the virtual convergence industry.

Article 22 (Implementation of Pilot Projects)
(1) The heads of central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments may implement pilot projects where they deem it necessary to promote the virtual convergence industry.
(2) The heads of central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments may provide necessary support to persons participating in pilot projects.
(3) The heads of central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments shall evaluate the performance of the pilot projects under paragraph (1).
(4) Matters necessary for the implementation, support, performance evaluation, etc. of pilot projects under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 23 (Support for Enterprises Excelling in Conversion to Virtual Convergence Services, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT may formulate support measures, such as selecting and granting awards to enterprises that have achieved outstanding results among those that have converted existing services, etc. into virtual convergence services, etc.
(2) Matters necessary for the selection and support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT.

Article 24 (Support for International Cooperation and Overseas Expansion)
(1) The Government may carry out the following projects to stimulate international cooperation related to the virtual convergence industry and promote entry into overseas markets:
1. International exchanges of information, technology, and personnel related to the virtual convergence industry;
2. Publicity, including exhibitions related to the virtual convergence industry, and overseas marketing;
3. Joint research and development between countries and international standardization of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc.;
4. Collection, analysis, and provision of information on overseas expansion related to the virtual convergence industry;
5. Attraction of investment related to the virtual convergence industry;
6. Other projects necessary to promote international cooperation and overseas expansion related to the virtual convergence industry.
(2) The Government may provide necessary budgetary support to persons participating in the projects specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1).

Article 25 (Use, etc. of Virtual Convergence Worlds by Heads of Central Administrative Agencies, etc.)
The heads of central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and the heads of public institutions shall actively utilize virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc. in performing the affairs under their jurisdiction.

Article 26 (Impact Assessment of Virtual Convergence Projects)
(1) The head of an institution prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a corporation or organization in which a central administrative agency, local government, or public institution has invested or to which it has contributed, shall, when undertaking a project related to the development, etc. of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc. (hereinafter referred to in this Article as a "virtual convergence project"), conduct an impact assessment of the virtual convergence project to analyze its impact on the private sector market before publishing a notice inviting bids; provided that this shall not apply where a virtual convergence project prescribed by Presidential Decree is undertaken.
(2) Matters necessary for the criteria, procedures, etc. for impact assessments of virtual convergence projects under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER V IMPROVEMENT OF REGULATIONS

Article 27 (Self-Regulation)
(1) An association may pursue self-regulation, including establishing and implementing a code of conduct or operating rules for virtual convergence business entities, to protect users and create a safe and reliable environment for the provision and use of virtual convergence technology or virtual convergence services, etc.
(2) An association may perform the following duties in connection with self-regulation under paragraph (1):
1. Establishment, amendment, and implementation of self-regulatory rules;
2. Education and publicity for virtual convergence business entities;
3. Voluntary inspections of the status of user protection by virtual convergence business entities and activities to improve such protection;
4. Other duties necessary to improve the level of user protection provided by member virtual convergence business entities.
(3) Where there is an association or organization related to an individual industrial sector that converges or integrates with the virtual convergence industry, an association shall endeavor to perform the duties under paragraph (2) in cooperation with that association or organization.
(4) The Government may support activities for self-regulation under paragraphs (1) through (3).

Article 28 (Interim Standards, Etc.)
(1) Where the Minister of Science and ICT determines, ex officio or upon reviewing a proposal from a virtual convergence business entity, an association, etc., that it is necessary to establish interim standards, the Minister may request the head of a relevant central administrative agency to establish or revise interim standards: Provided, That where it is difficult to identify the relevant central administrative agency, the Minister of Science and ICT may establish interim standards.
(2) A person who intends to propose the establishment of interim standards shall submit to the Minister of Science and ICT an application for interim standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT, accompanied by documents concerning the content of the interim standards, the need therefor, measures to protect users, etc.
(3) The head of a relevant central administrative agency who receives a request under paragraph (1) shall promptly establish interim standards: Provided, That where there are special circumstances preventing the head of the relevant central administrative agency from complying with the request of the Minister of Science and ICT, the head shall notify the Minister of Science and ICT of the reasons therefor in writing without delay.
(4) When establishing interim standards, the head of a relevant central administrative agency may specify their period of validity, scope of application, etc.
(5) The head of a relevant central administrative agency shall finalize the interim standards prepared under paragraph (3) following deliberation and resolution by the Strategy Committee. In such cases, where necessary to ensure safety, protect users, etc. in relation to the interim standards, the Strategy Committee may recommend that the head of the relevant central administrative agency take necessary measures, such as testing and verification concerning the assurance of safety, user protection, etc. in relation to those interim standards.
(6) The head of a relevant central administrative agency shall publicly announce the interim standards finalized under paragraph (5).
(7) Other matters concerning the procedures, methods, etc. for the establishment, etc. of interim standards shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 29 (Management of Interim Standards, Etc.)
(1) After publicly announcing interim standards under Article 28 (6), the head of a relevant central administrative agency shall endeavor to enact or amend statutes and regulations where necessary to clarify the meaning of the statutes and regulations relating thereto.
(2) Where interim standards cease to have effect as a result of the enactment or amendment of statutes and regulations, etc. relating to those standards, the head of a relevant central administrative agency shall take measures to minimize damage to business activities subject to the interim standards, unless there are special circumstances.
(3) Where serious hazards, etc. relating to safety, user protection, etc. are discovered during the implementation of interim standards, the head of a relevant central administrative agency may, in consultation with the Minister of Science and ICT, suspend the application of the interim standards for a specified period or revoke the interim standards.
(4) The Minister of Science and ICT and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may jointly manage and supervise the testing and verification of interim standards and the projects, etc. relating thereto.

CHAPTER VI PROTECTION OF USERS, ETC.

Article 30 (Protection of Users)
(1) The Government may carry out the following projects to protect the rights and interests of users:
1. Provision of information and education to users concerning virtual convergence services, etc.;
2. Education and training for virtual convergence business entities concerning user protection;
3. Protection of children and juveniles from harmful conduct and harmful media materials within virtual convergence worlds;
4. Formulation and implementation of other policies to prevent and provide relief for harm suffered by users.
(2) The Government shall investigate the occurrence or likelihood of physical or mental harm to users.
(3) Virtual convergence business entities shall take necessary measures to prevent harm to the life, body, health, or property of users.

Article 31 (Creation of a Sound Virtual Convergence World Ecosystem, Etc.)
(1) The Government shall endeavor to protect the rights and interests of users and to create and maintain a sound virtual convergence world ecosystem.
(2) Virtual convergence business entities shall endeavor not to produce, distribute, disseminate, post, display, reproduce, transmit, etc. content that is unjustifiably discriminatory with respect to sex, politics, the economy, society, culture, etc., in order to create and maintain a sound virtual convergence world ecosystem: Provided, That in the case of a virtual convergence business entity that qualifies as an online service provider under the Copyright Act, such efforts shall not be directed at monitoring or investigation under Article 102 (3) of the Copyright Act.
(3) A virtual convergence platform operator whose sales revenue, number of users, etc. meet the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree shall establish procedures to resolve disputes between users and the virtual convergence platform operator or among users concerning violations of statutes and regulations, terms and conditions, operating policies, etc.
(4) Virtual convergence platform operators shall operate their platforms transparently and fairly, and shall endeavor to avoid unjustifiably discriminatory treatment of users.
(5) Virtual convergence platform operators shall endeavor to improve the quality and performance of their platforms and their levels of information protection and security, and to ensure compatibility, interoperability, and the sustainability of services.

CHAPTER VII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 32 (Hearings)
The Minister of Science and ICT shall hold a hearing when intending to make any of the following dispositions:
1. Revocation of the designation of a dedicated agency under Article 17 (4);
2. Revocation of the designation of a support center under Article 19 (4).

Article 33 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority and Duties)
(1) Part of the authority of the Minister of Science and ICT under this Act may be delegated to the heads of affiliated agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Minister of Science and ICT may entrust part of the duties under this Act to relevant institutions, organizations, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 34 (Deemed Status as Public Officials for Purposes of Applying Penalty Provisions)
The officers and employees of any of the following institutions, corporations, or organizations shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Article 127 and Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act:
1. An institution or organization performing duties entrusted by the Government under Article 11 (2);
2. An institution or organization performing duties entrusted by the Government under Article 13 (3);
3. A dedicated agency designated by the Minister of Science and ICT under Article 17 (1);
4. A support center designated by the Minister of Science and ICT under Article 19 (1);
5. An institution or organization performing duties entrusted by the Minister of Science and ICT under Article 33 (2).

Article 35 (Exemption from Liability)
Where a public official or employee of a central administrative agency, local government, or public institution proactively performs duties to improve regulations under this Act, including those concerning interim standards under Article 28, and the conduct involves neither intentional misconduct nor gross negligence, the public official or employee shall not be held liable through disciplinary action, censure, etc. under the Act on Public Sector Audits for the results of such performance.

ADDENDA <Act No. 20352, February 27, 2024>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date on which six months have elapsed since its promulgation.

Article 2 (Amendment of Another Act)
The Special Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Technology, Vitalization of Convergence Thereof, Etc. is partially amended as follows:

In Article 7 (3), subparagraph 8 is renumbered as subparagraph 9, and a new subparagraph 8 is inserted in the same paragraph as follows:

8. Major matters concerning the promotion of the virtual convergence industry under the Virtual Convergence Industry Promotion Act.
